transcript.content: hi, i’m berry. tell me about your dream, however it comes back to you.
The first thing that comes back is the library. It was so quiet, and the water started coming in under the doors.
there's something about water in a quiet library that feels almost rude, like it doesn't belong there at all. did it come in fast or just slowly, like it had all the time in the world?
Slowly, I think. It didn't rush in, it just kept rising. No sound to it either.
no sound at all. that quiet water almost makes it worse. where were you in the room while it was rising?
I was just standing there, I think near the middle. Watching it. The desks were still there at first.
near the middle, watching something that shouldn't be happening. what was it like seeing the desks still there, before they went under?
It felt wrong. Like everything was normal except the water. And then it got up over the desk tops, and the books started floating off.
the books floating off — that image stays with me. were you just watching them go, or did you feel like you should do something?
I didn't try to do anything. It was too late for that. They were opening like birds, just drifting around.
books opening like birds is such a gentle ruin. did any of them come near you?

I don't remember any coming close to me. Just up and away.

Then my sister was there. In the little yellow rowing boat.
your sister just appears, already in a boat, like she knew. did she call to you, or just row over?
She just told me to get in. She was calm, like it was normal. I climbed in.
calm in the middle of a flooding library. as the water rose, could you see where you were headed?
We rowed between the shelves. I don't think we had a destination yet, not until we went up to the round window.
up to a round window. was it already open, or did you have to do something to get through?
She opened it. It wasn't open before.
she knew exactly what to do. what did you see through it when it opened?
It was morning outside. The whole city underwater, just rooftops and the tops of trees. Then I woke up.
you went from quiet water inside to a whole world gone under, and then it just ends. even now, does the feeling of it stay with you?
Yeah, it does. It was strange, but not scary really. I keep thinking about the whale.
the whale. tell me about the whale. where did it come in?
It swam past us under the water while we were in the boat. It was huge, filled the whole aisle. And it didn't scare me at all.

so in your dream, you were in a quiet library, standing near the middle, while water came slowly in under the doors without a sound. it rose past the desks, and the books floated off, opening like birds. your sister appeared in a little yellow rowing boat, calm, and you got in. as she rowed between the shelves, a huge whale swam past underneath, filling the whole aisle, and you weren't scared at all. she rowed you up to a round window, opened it, and outside it was morning with the whole city underwater, just rooftops and treetops. then you woke up.

did i get that right, or is there anything i missed?
That's basically it. The only thing missing is the very start in the reading room with the green glass lamp on every desk and shelves up to the ceiling. But the rest is right.

so it begins in the reading room, green glass lamps on every desk, shelves up to the ceiling.

have i got the start right now?
Yes, that's right.

i feel like i have your dream now. the green lamps, the silent water, the whale, your sister and the yellow boat, the city gone under.

would you like me to draw it for you?
Yes, I'd like that.

there are a few ways i could draw it. a soft watercolor, like a memory of rain. an old woodcut print, like a story cut into wood. a quiet lithograph, like dust settling on a remembered afternoon. or just how it looked, like a snapshot from deep inside a dream. which feels closest, or would you describe your own?

A quiet lithograph. That feels closest.

Hmm.

a quiet lithograph it is. i'll start with the reading room and let the dream come back to me.

and since you're in the dream, i'll draw you in it too.

would you like to be drawn as you are — you can tell me a little about yourself — or should i draw you as i imagine you from the dream?
Draw me as you imagine me from the dream.

i'm sketching you and your sister, the whale, the reading room, the library aisles, the outside world, and the little yellow rowing boat now. everything will appear on the right over the next minute or two. you can tell me if anything looks wrong once it's there.
Okay, I'll take a look.
does it look the way you remember it?
The reading room is right with the lamps and shelves, and the library aisle with the whale looks right too.
i'm glad the reading room and the whale feel right. the rest is still taking shape.
The rest looks right too.

that's all of them, then. everyone and everything is sketched.

i'll draw the moments of the dream in order now, each one carrying on from the ones before it. they'll appear on the right as they're ready.
Okay, I see the first few.

they're appearing one by one.

do the ones you can see look the way you remember them?
Yes, the ones I can see look right. I'm curious about the rest.

i'm glad those first few feel right.

the rest are still being drawn — they'll appear on the right soon.
I see the new one. It looks right so far.

once you say it looks right, the next moments will be drawn from there.

does the water rising over the desk tops look the way you remember?
Yes, the water over the desk tops looks right. That's when the books start drifting up.
good, the water over the desk tops is right. the books drifting up are part of it.
I can see the books adrift now, and that's right too.

the books adrift being right is good to hear. the next moments will carry on from when you climbed into the boat, so they'll be drawn once that part looks right too.

does the dreamer climbing into the boat look the way you remember?
I don't see that picture yet. Only the five from before.

oh, the boat one is actually in that set of five already — it's the one with you climbing in. maybe give it a second to show up on your screen.

the other three are still being drawn, they'll be on the right soon.
Now I see it. Yes, it looks right. The boat is yellow and the library is around us.

the yellow boat in the library, that's right.

then there's the moment you wanted to pause on: the huge whale filling the whole aisle, swimming past underwater, and it didn't scare you at all. once that's right, the next moments will be drawn from there. is that how you saw it?
The whale picture isn't up yet. But the climbing into the boat one looks right.

i'm glad the boat picture looks right. the whale one should show up on the right in just a moment.

i need to tell you, though — one of the moments couldn't be drawn because of a problem on our side. it's the one where you rowed between the shelves with no destination yet. i'm sorry about that; it won't be included.
That's okay. I remember that part without it.

that's okay. you'll have that part with you anyway.

the sister opening the round window is up on the right now — does it look the way you remember?
I can see the sister opening the window, and that looks right. She looks calm like in the dream.

i'm glad the sister opening the window looks right. so that's 7 of the 8 moments, all on the right now, and the one with the rowing couldn't be drawn because of a problem on our side — i'm sorry about that. thank you for sharing this dream with me. it was a gift to walk through it with you. you can look through all of it there.
